author: nshchego
title: ARM64 cross-compilation build fails with cc1plus invalid-pch error on shared cmake_pch.hxx.gch
signature: cc1plus: error: cmake_pch.hxx.gch: not a PCH file [-Werror=invalid-pch]|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: Build / Build
failed_jobs.symptom: cc1plus fails with '-Werror=invalid-pch' because cmake_pch.hxx.gch for openvino_reference is not a valid PCH file after the build directory is reconfigured for a secondary build pass

failed_jobs.name: ci/gha_overall_status_ubuntu_22_arm64_cross_compilation
failed_jobs.symptom: Overall status check fails because the Build job failed

key_errors: cc1plus: error: /__w/openvino/openvino/openvino/openvino_build/src/core/reference/CMakeFiles/openvino_reference.dir/cmake_pch.hxx.gch: not a PCH file [-Werror=invalid-pch]
cc1plus: all warnings being treated as errors
root_cause: The ARM64 cross-compilation job reconfigures the same CMake build directory in-place with different cache variables for a secondary packaging/bindings build pass, which triggers a rebuild of the openvino_reference target. The previously generated precompiled header object (cmake_pch.hxx.gch) under the same CMakeFiles directory becomes stale/incompatible for the new compiler invocation, and GCC rejects it as 'not a PCH file'. Because -Werror (CMAKE_COMPILE_WARNING_AS_ERROR=ON) is enabled, this escalates to a hard build failure for every compiled reference op. This is the same job-agnostic infrastructure defect recorded 5 times previously against this workflow; the commit under investigation (#38611, GPU Coverity fixes) is unrelated to the failure and merely the first merge-queue commit to hit the pre-existing, unresolved CI defect again.
reproduction_steps: Not reliably reproducible outside CI without the exact ARM64 cross-compilation Docker image and cache state; locally: configure+build the main target, then re-run 'cmake -UTBB* -S <repo> -B <same-build-dir> -DCPACK_GENERATOR=NPM -DENABLE_SYSTEM_TBB=OFF -DENABLE_WHEEL=OFF' followed by 'cmake --build <same-build-dir>' and observe cc1plus reject the cached src/core/reference/CMakeFiles/openvino_reference.dir/cmake_pch.hxx.gch as an invalid PCH file.
recommended_actions: Use a separate build directory for the secondary (JS/NPM) cmake reconfigure instead of reusing BUILD_DIR, so the openvino_reference PCH is generated fresh for the new configuration
Explicitly remove/regenerate cmake_pch.hxx.gch (and other PCH artifacts) before or during the second cmake --build invocation in the ARM64 cross-compilation workflow step

Consider disabling precompiled headers (ENABLE_FASTER_BUILD=OFF) for the secondary reconfigure pass, or passing -DCMAKE_COMPILE_WARNING_AS_ERROR=OFF for that specific sub-build to avoid escalating stale-PCH warnings into hard failures

Escalate as a known, unresolved infrastructure issue against job_build_linux.yml for the ubuntu_22_arm64_cross_compilation workflow — this is now the 6th recorded occurrence since 2026-09-25 and remains unfixed
prevention_strategies: Avoid reconfiguring and rebuilding the same CMake build directory with different cache variables (TBB/wheel toggles) in sequential steps of the same job when precompiled headers are enabled; isolate secondary packaging builds (JS/NPM, wheels) into their own build directories, or explicitly invalidate PCH artifacts between reconfigures. Add a CI guard that detects 'not a PCH file' errors and automatically cleans stale .gch files before retrying.
historical_context: Identical failure signature recorded 5 times previously in this database: runs 36123294303 (2026-09-25), 37391757947, 37394029538, 37410819403, and 37421582585 (all 2026-10-06), all on the same 'Linux (Ubuntu 22.04, ARM64 cross-compilation, Python 3.11)' workflow with the same cc1plus invalid-pch cmake_pch.hxx.gch error. This is now the 6th occurrence; the defect in the shared build-directory PCH reuse remains unresolved and should be escalated as a persistent CI infra bug rather than investigated as a code regression each time.
